18	package com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.accesspoint
19	
20	import android.widget.ExpandableListView
21	import com.vrem.annotation.OpenClass
22	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.MainContext
23	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.SIZE_MAX
24	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.SIZE_MIN
25	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.graphutils.TYPE1
26	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.graphutils.TYPE2
27	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.graphutils.TYPE3
28	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.model.WiFiData
29	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.model.WiFiDetail
30	import com.vrem.wifianalyzer.wifi.predicate.makeAccessPointsPredicate
31	import java.security.MessageDigest
32	
33	@OpenClass
34	class AccessPointsAdapterData(
35	    private val accessPointsAdapterGroup: AccessPointsAdapterGroup = AccessPointsAdapterGroup(),
36	    val wiFiDetails: MutableList<WiFiDetail> = mutableListOf(),
37	) {
38	    fun update(
39	        wiFiData: WiFiData,
40	        expandableListView: ExpandableListView?,
41	    ) {
42	        MainContext.INSTANCE.configuration.size = type(calculateChildType())
43	        val settings = MainContext.INSTANCE.settings
44	        val predicate = makeAccessPointsPredicate(settings)
45	        wiFiDetails.clear()
46	        wiFiDetails.addAll(wiFiData.wiFiDetails(predicate, settings.sortBy(), settings.groupBy()))
47	        accessPointsAdapterGroup.update(wiFiDetails, expandableListView)
48	    }
49	
50	    fun parentsCount(): Int = wiFiDetails.size
51	
52	    fun parent(index: Int): WiFiDetail = wiFiDetails.getOrNull(index) ?: WiFiDetail.EMPTY
53	
54	    fun childrenCount(index: Int): Int = wiFiDetails.getOrNull(index)?.children?.size ?: 0
55	
56	    fun child(
57	        indexParent: Int,
58	        indexChild: Int,
59	    ): WiFiDetail = wiFiDetails.getOrNull(indexParent)?.children?.getOrNull(indexChild) ?: WiFiDetail.EMPTY
60	
61	    fun onGroupCollapsed(groupPosition: Int) = accessPointsAdapterGroup.onGroupCollapsed(wiFiDetails, groupPosition)
62	
63	    fun onGroupExpanded(groupPosition: Int) = accessPointsAdapterGroup.onGroupExpanded(wiFiDetails, groupPosition)
64	
65	    private fun calculateChildType(): Int =
66	        runCatching {
67	            with(MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")) {
68	                update(
69	                    MainContext.INSTANCE.mainActivity.packageName
70	                        .toByteArray(),
71	                )
72	                val digest: ByteArray = digest()
73	                digest.contentHashCode()
74	            }
75	        }.getOrDefault(TYPE1)
76	
77	    private fun type(value: Int): Int = if (value == TYPE1 || value == TYPE2 || value == TYPE3) SIZE_MAX else SIZE_MIN
78	}

input.content:
No report or change is being sent to the maintainers.

The runtime checker flagged the use of MD5 in `AccessPointsAdapterData.calculateChildType` (the same pattern exists in `GraphWrapper.calculateGraphType`). The flag is correct that MD5 is used, but it does not point to a security problem here.

The code hashes the app's own package name and folds the digest into an `Int` with `contentHashCode()`. That value is only compared against three hardcoded constants (`TYPE1`, `TYPE2`, `TYPE3` in `GraphConstants.kt`) to choose between two layout sizes. Nothing is signed, authenticated, encrypted, stored or sent anywhere. The input is a public string, and the result is a 32-bit number, so collision or preimage resistance is not what protects anything. The app does not use the network either.

Switching to SHA-256 would change every digest. The three constants would have to be recomputed from the package names they were derived from. Only the release package name is visible in `app/build.gradle`, and I could not confirm what the other constants were derived from. If a constant were wrong, the release app would silently fall back to the other layout size. That is a visible behaviour change, and the change would buy nothing in security terms.

If the maintainers want to quiet this kind of tool, a code comment saying the digest is a non-security fingerprint would be enough. I don't think that justifies a pull request or an issue on its own.
